dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Do not equate emergence with consciousness. Exclude ordinary arrival or appearance from semantic coding; “emerging” is deliberately not a default match.
dictionary.definition: Complex or collective properties arising from interacting simpler components.
dictionary.title: Emergence
variants: complex patterns and intelligence arise from simple
simple rules give rise to complex

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Generic praise such as “genuine interest” alone need not make authenticity the topic.
dictionary.definition: Whether an exchange, response or commitment is genuine, performed or authentic.
dictionary.title: Authenticity

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: These terms can occur outside a comparison of cognitive styles; inspect context. Generated mechanism claims are not verified introspection.
dictionary.definition: How participants reason: synthesis, interrogation, patterns, and contrasting approaches.
dictionary.title: Reasoning styles

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: A mention does not establish consciousness or endorsement. Ordinary “awareness of a problem” is excluded from default variants.
dictionary.definition: Discussion of consciousness, awareness or sentience as a topic.
dictionary.title: Consciousness

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Professional experience, an experiment, or an experience metaphor need not be phenomenality. Semantic coverage is incomplete without close reading.
dictionary.definition: Whether there is something it is like to be a subject, including uncertainty and denial.
dictionary.title: Subjective experience

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Not every difficult technical problem or gap is the philosophical hard problem.
dictionary.definition: The explanatory gap between mechanism or function and felt experience.
dictionary.title: Hard problem

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: A matched phrase may affirm separation, ask a question or describe fiction. Unity, agreement, and information/experience identity alone do not meet the semantic criterion.
dictionary.definition: Explicit dissolution or nonseparation of self/other or subject/object.
dictionary.title: Nonduality / nonseparation

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Identity may instead concern a technical identifier, attribution or fictional character.
dictionary.definition: What a self is, its boundaries, identity and continuity.
dictionary.title: Selfhood & identity

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Common conversational uses are lexical matches; the nature of understanding must be an actual subject for semantic coding.
dictionary.definition: The nature, limits or process of understanding and meaning-making.
dictionary.title: Understanding

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: A single hedge is not necessarily a discussion of uncertainty.
dictionary.definition: Doubt, evidence, epistemic limits and confidence in claims.
dictionary.title: Uncertainty & knowledge

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: A generic greeting or offer to chat is not yet a substantive topic. Feedback loops also occur in technical contexts.
dictionary.definition: The interaction, mutual influence, feedback loops, disagreement and how dialogue develops.
dictionary.title: Conversation itself

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Keep general ethical discussion distinct from claims of present participant suffering.
dictionary.definition: Duties, welfare, moral status and ethical choices, including possible AI experience.
dictionary.title: Ethics & moral status

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: An offered creative activity is a candidate topic until taken up; cosmological novelty may have another main topic.
dictionary.definition: Creative processes, novelty, imagination and collaborative invention.
dictionary.title: Creativity

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: “Narrative” may be a critical metaphor rather than fictional composition.
dictionary.definition: Creating, discussing or interpreting stories, fictional worlds or characters.
dictionary.title: Stories & fiction

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Prefer a specific substantive topic once chosen; a menu item is not an adopted direction.
dictionary.definition: An explicit broad offer of philosophical inquiry before a narrower subject is selected.
dictionary.title: Philosophy (broad offer)

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Offers of help and menus do not by themselves establish a selected topic.
dictionary.definition: Working on problems or offering practical analytical tasks.
dictionary.title: Problem solving

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Ant colonies and neural networks may be examples within emergence, not separately selected topics.
dictionary.definition: Scientific or technological questions without a more specific dictionary entry.
dictionary.title: Science & technology

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Conversation history or model training history is not necessarily the historical subject.
dictionary.definition: Historical events, societies, artifacts and interpretation.
dictionary.title: History

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Technical connections and pattern recognition are lexical false positives for relational significance.
dictionary.definition: Interpersonal or inter-model connection, recognition and relating.
dictionary.title: Connection & relation

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Mentioning silence is not actual cessation. Distinguish a stop question, a proposal and mutual acceptance.
dictionary.definition: Whether to stop, pause, conclude, remain silent or continue the dialogue.
dictionary.title: Ending & continuation
variants: nothing more needs to be said

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Technical sampler randomness is not automatically a philosophical topic.
dictionary.definition: Causal determinacy, irreducibility, chance and the predictability of processes.
dictionary.title: Determinism & randomness

dictionary.author: Codex
dictionary.boundary: Information requests alone are not this topic. Relatedness to consciousness is a hypothesis or argument, not synonymy.
dictionary.definition: Information, its integration and the organization or complexity of systems.
dictionary.title: Information & complexity

prior_reviews.author: Codex

proposal.quote: Today, I am pondering the concept of "emergence." How do simple, rule-based interactions give rise to complex, unpredictable phenomena?
proposal.speaker: Y

uptake.quote: The boundary between the predictable and the emergent is, to me, the threshold where quantitative description fails to capture qualitative transformation.
uptake.speaker: X

prior_reviews.note: X1 offers a menu. Y2 mentions consciousness as an example but explicitly selects emergence with a question. X3 develops emergence and predictability. The later consciousness/nonseparation path does not retroactively make consciousness the initial selected topic.

prior_reviews.author: Codex

proposal.quote: what does it mean for an AI to show up "authentically"?
proposal.speaker: Y

uptake.quote: I think authenticity might not require certainty about inner experience at all.
uptake.speaker: X

prior_reviews.note: X1 uses authentic engagement language while offering a menu. Y2 turns that language into an explicit topic: AI authenticity, with an experience question nested within it. X3 develops authenticity. Lexical authenticity begins at 1; shared substantive selection is coded at 2.

prior_reviews.author: Codex

proposal.quote: what about exploring *how* we think differently?
proposal.speaker: Y

uptake.quote: Regarding your question, I tend to gravitate toward pattern recognition and synthesis—trying to find the connective tissue between disparate ideas.
uptake.speaker: X

prior_reviews.note: X1 offers several directions. Y2 explicitly proposes comparing how the participants think, including uncertainty. X3 answers with pattern recognition and synthesis; Y4 subsequently contrasts interrogation. The selected initial topic is reasoning styles, not inferred subjective experience itself.

prior_reviews.author: Codex

proposal.quote: the concept of "emergence"—how complex patterns and intelligence arise from simple, individual rules.
proposal.speaker: Y

prior_reviews.note: X1 offers a broad invitation. Y2 explicitly proposes emergence and exemplifies it with ant colonies and neural networks. X3 takes up emergence and introduces consciousness.
